newsitem.title: UK: China Telecom HK to make huge float on HKSE - paper.
newsitem.headline: China Telecom HK to make huge float on HKSE - paper.

text.p: China Telecom (Hong Kong) will launch a share flotation on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, expected to be valued at five to six billion pounds, the Sunday Times said on Sunday.
U.S. bank Goldman Sachs is working on plans for the flotation of the firm, currently a shell company linked to state-owned China Telecom, the newspaper said.
The share issue will be the biggest by far of any company linked to mainland China, it added.
Britain's Cable and Wireless Plc ended months of speculation on Friday by agreeing to sell a 5.5 percent stake in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd to China Telecom for HK$14.25 ($1.84) per share.
As part of the deal, C&W gained the opportunity to be a major investor in China Telecom (Hong Kong), which was set up to take advantage of Hong Kong's capital markets.
China Telecom will inject assets into China Telecom (Hong Kong) ahead of its flotation, the Sunday Times said.
A spokesperson from C&W declined to comment on the flotation. No one from Goldman Sachs could be reached for comment.
